description: Over the #755 arena: no fact true at every accessible world strictly suffices for a contingent fact. Any reason-closed founded account of a contingent fact has a reason that does not strictly suffice, is not contrast-relevant, and has a noncontingent reason for a contingent member. Three models delete one member each. In ground the source is necessary and admitted for a contingent target without sufficing; the account is closed and founded and not contrast-relevant. In relocated a contingent act is admitted for a contingent effect, suffices for it and is false at each world lacking it; the account is closed and founded, and every reason for the act holds at a world lacking the act, its reason being a necessary source that does not suffice for it, so the account is not contrast-relevant. In necessitarian the source is necessary, admitted and sufficing, no fact is contingent, the account is closed and founded, all its reasons necessitate, and contrast relevance holds vacuously. Admission as a reason does not imply strict sufficiency, and the first statement fires only on strict sufficiency. Models show satisfiability and none is a reading of divine simplicity; no standard is asserted, and no branch is excluded or preferred. No root premise is established.
